analyst_view.overall: Bodø/Glimt sit 25th of 36 with 4 points from 4 games, so this home game on the Aspmyra artificial pitch is close to a must-win to stay in the play-off places; LASK are 16th with 6 points. Bodø are also in a tight Eliteserien title race (level on points and goal difference with Viking at the start of November, season ends 6 December), and early in the month they had an illness in the squad plus injuries to goalkeepers Faye Lund and Sjong, Hakon Evjen (knee) and August Mikkelsen (groin); I found no fresh update on those, and the numbers list no absences for either side. LASK have played every three days this autumn (eight games in 24 days at one point) and Dietmar Kühbauer has been rotating in the league. No referee is named yet. News for this match was thin, so the view rests on form and context and stays with the numbers everywhere.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.8 goals (2.7 Bodø, 1.1 LASK), a high total built on Bodø's strong home record on their artificial pitch and LASK's recent scoring run (18 in their last 6, already counted as +2.9% for them). Bodø need the win and play on the front foot at home, but that is what the numbers already expect; with no confirmed news on Evjen or Mikkelsen I stay at 3.8.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.4 corners, with Bodø taking more (5.9) as the side likely to have the ball. LASK's busy schedule could tire them late on, but nothing confirmed points to a change in either side's approach, so I stay at about 10.4.
